# EasySweep

> A Mac cleaner: it reclaims disk space from app caches, developer data and AI
> tool data, uninstalls applications along with the files they leave behind, finds
> large, old and duplicate files, and monitors the system. macOS 14+. Free, with a
> one-time Pro upgrade from $9.99.

EasySweep finds the disk space apps and tools quietly consume in folders Finder
never shows — every app's caches, `~/Library/Developer`, package manager caches,
AI models and session data — and lets the user delete it selectively. The
Overview opens with only the Safe level ticked; every other page opens with
nothing ticked.

## Editions

- **Direct download** (recommended): unsandboxed, notarized DMG. Reaches every
  catalogued location without asking. Can remove an application bundle outright.
  Pro sold as a licence key, in tiers covering 1, 2, or 3 Macs
  ($9.99 / $14.99 / $19.99); a seat is freed by deactivating a Mac.
- **Mac App Store**: the same app, sandboxed as Apple requires. Asks for home
  folder access once per section, and usually cannot delete another app's
  bundle — the user drags that to the Trash. Pro sold as an in-app purchase
  tied to the Apple Account, with no device limit.

## What it cleans

Four sections: Caches (every installed app's caches, grouped by app, 400+
catalogued locations across all sections), Developer (Xcode caches, Derived Data,
Device Support, simulators and runtimes, package manager and toolchain caches),
App Data (AI models, session history and attachments — data that does not
regenerate), and System (logs, crash reports, wallpapers and update leftovers).
The Overview offers three levels — Safe, Balanced and Deep — across all of them.
Users can add their own folders as custom categories (Pro).

## Other tools

- Applications: uninstall apps with their leftovers, matched by confidence;
  everything goes to the Trash, with Undo. Orphaned files of removed apps too.
- Utilities: Large & Old Files, Duplicate Files (byte-identical, one copy always
  kept), Finder Metadata (.DS_Store) and Project Caches. Scanning is free; moving
  to the Trash is Pro.
- App Updates: lists apps that are behind (App Store, Homebrew, MacPorts,
  Sparkle) and updates them.
- Startup Items: login items and background helpers.
- System Monitor: live CPU, GPU, memory, network and disk activity, with
  optional menu bar indicators.
- Activity: a history of every clean, manual or automatic.
- Auto Clean (Pro): per-item rules by size or low free space, optionally only
  files older than a day, week or month.

Excluded on purpose: lockfiles, SDK installs, emulator images, editor workspace
state, credentials, browser history and passwords. Those are not caches.

## Safety properties

- Section pages open with nothing ticked; the Overview ticks only Safe.
- Refuses to delete any folder containing its own bundle; symlinks are skipped.
- Unreadable folders are reported as failures, never shown as empty.
- Simulators are deleted through Apple's `simctl`, never by removing folders.
- Sizes are allocated blocks, matching `du` — the space actually reclaimed.
- Uninstalls, duplicates and utility finds move to the Trash, so they are reversible.
- The one-click clean can never reach simulators, archives or AI session history.

## Privacy

No analytics, no telemetry, no account. The free app makes no network requests
at all. Pro optionally syncs category and rule definitions through iCloud, and a
direct licence is validated against Polar. Scan results never leave the
Mac.
